To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the kallikrine-kinin system and the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system are antagonistic, and that prostaglandins may be the link between the two systems.

(1) the kallikren-kinin system and prostaglandin synthesis are interrelated in the kidney and (2) this interrelation may be directed to the facilitation of renal salt-water excretion in states in which salt balance is positive.
kinins and prostacyclin are involved in renal regulation of salt and water homeostasis and that their interaction may be directed to facilitate the excretion of salt and water.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the interaction of mineralocorticoid hormones and the renal kinn-kinin system with particular reference to their influence on renal hemodynamics, excretory events, and the intrarenal production of prostaglandin-like substances.
the interaction between the kallikren-kinin system and the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and the role of prostaglandin E2 in the regulation of renal function.
the interaction of mineralocorticoid hormones with renal prostaglandin and the renal kalliikrein- kinin systems and the role of these interactions in the regulation of salt-water balance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mineralocorticoid excess results in an increased intrarenal release of prostagladins of the E and F series and a concomitant enhancement of the kallkirein-kinin activity.
mineralocorticoids stimulate renal kallikren-kinin system which then stimulates prostaglandin synthesis.
the kallikrene-kinin system and PGEs are interrelated and that the interrelation may be a physiological mechanism for the regulation of renal hemodynamics and excretory function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
kinins and prostanoids interact in the renal circulation to reinforce the natriuretic effect of kinins and the diuretic effect of prostanoids.
kinins and prostacyclin (PGI2) have the capacity of influencing renal hemodynamic and tubular events and may interact so as to reinforce each other.
the kallikrine-kinin system is a major component of the renal regulation of sodium and water balance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction of kinins, prostaglandins, and mineralocorticoids is a complex and multifaceted process.

the kallikren-kinin system and prostaglandin system are interdependent, with one system influencing the other and the interaction between them is directed to the facilitation of renal sodium and water excretion.
the kallikren-kinin system is a potent regulator of renal sodium handling and is an important counterbalancing system in the face of mineralocorticoid excess.
